title: [AUG-183] Live action items: stop dedup from deleting distinct items
why_we_need_this:
Bug found on 2026-11-03 in dev (session "Recording 03.11.2026, 15:58:17", id ac0169f7-c216-4ab2-8346-e3a6e9b3e062, ~58 min, dual track). About 10 real action items were extracted during the live recording, but while new items appeared the older ones vanished; the final session kept only 1 item (@server/data/sessions/ac0169f7-c216-4ab2-8346-e3a6e9b3e062/action-items.json).

Root cause (from the dev server log): the local-model dedup in @server/src/services/liveActionItems.ts (LiveActionItemsExtractor.localDedupTick every 20 s, DEDUP_SYSTEM_PROMPT) returns merge/delete operations for DIFFERENT tasks, and applyDedupOps applies every operation whose ids exist — there is no check that two merged items are really the same task, and the small local model may also delete any unlocked item. Log pattern: "cloud call #35: +1 new, 3 total" → "local dedup: 2/2 op(s) applied" → next line "1 total"; "local fallback #4: +3 new, 5 total" → "local dedup: 3/4 op(s) applied" → "2 total". About 14 items were added over the meeting and about 13 were removed by dedup. The lost items cannot be recovered from files (only the final list is persisted).

User decision (2026-11-03): guard dedup — the local model may only merge, never delete; a merge is applied only when the two texts are actually close (server-side word-overlap check); the cloud (Groq) dedup operations go through the same guard. Distinct items must always survive. Without this fix live action items are useless in long meetings: users lose agreed tasks silently.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Local dedup (localDedupTick) never removes an item through a delete operation: delete ops from the local model are ignored (not applied, not counted as applied).
- [ ] A merge operation (local or cloud) is applied only when the server-side similarity check between the two item texts passes (normalized word overlap, threshold as a named exported constant); a merge of two different tasks is skipped.
- [ ] Cloud (Groq) dedup ops go through the same merge guard; cloud delete ops are either guarded or dropped — the chosen rule is stated in a code comment and in the live-transcription route.
- [ ] Existing rules stay: locked/manual items are never removed; in a merge the edited item survives; both edited → skipped; exact-duplicate skip on add is unchanged.
- [ ] The log line shows guarded ops separately, e.g. "[actionItems] local dedup: 1/3 op(s) applied, 2 rejected by guard" — no transcript or item text in logs.
- [ ] Existing server tests pass (cd server && npm test); existing tests that assert the old unguarded behaviour are adjusted only as far as the new rule requires. No new tests unless the user asks.
- [ ] Manual check on a live recording of at least 10 minutes with several distinct commitments: all distinct items remain in the live panel and in the saved session (Windows; macOS check noted as pending if not run).
- [ ] project-context/transcription/live-transcription/README.md (Action items section and Invariants) describes the guard.
important_constraints:
- Server-only change in @server/src/services/liveActionItems.ts; do not change the extraction gate, rate limits, local fallback scheduling or the WebSocket protocol.
- Platform-neutral code (Windows + macOS); no process.platform branches needed.
- Do not log transcript or action item text.
- Do not touch AUG-182 files (client live panel / compact widgets) — that task is separate and has uncommitted changes in the working tree.
- Do not write new tests unless the user explicitly asks (project rule).

## Scope added by the user (2026-11-03)
Live items came out in English for a Russian meeting (pre-existing, seen before the dedup fix). Fixed here: speechLanguage() detects the speech script and both extraction payloads (Groq + local) pass "language"; the prompts require item text in that language. Latin / short speech → no hint.
